draft.title: Frameworks of ideas
card: In VCE English, the Creating texts area asks you to write your own texts. Your writing is built around one framework of ideas.
A framework of ideas is a broad area to explore, such as country, protest, personal journeys or play. It gives your writing a focus, but it does not tell you what to say.
You explore the framework through your own ideas and choices. Two students can use the same framework and write very different texts.
Your text is written for a purpose and an audience, and it can take a form such as a short story, a speech or a personal essay. The framework is the area of ideas the text explores.
draft.remember: A framework is a broad area of ideas. Your text explores it in your own way.

a.q: What is the main job of a framework of ideas in Creating texts?
opts: It gives your writing an area of ideas to explore
It gives you the exact argument to put in your text
It sets the form your text must take, such as a speech
It lists the techniques your text must include
a.why: A framework is a broad area of ideas, and the student decides how to explore it. It does not fix the argument, the form or the techniques, which are the writer's choices.
a.clue: Think of the framework as a topic area, not a set of instructions.

b.q: Priya and Tom both build their texts around the framework of play. Priya writes a story about a childhood cricket game. Tom writes a speech about why adults need time to be playful. What does this show?
opts: One framework can lead to very different texts
Play must be explored through a story and not a speech
Two texts on one framework must reach the same conclusion
A framework only suits texts about sport and games
b.why: Both texts explore play, but they differ in form, focus and ideas. This shows a framework leaves room for the writer's own choices. It does not fix the form or the conclusion.
b.clue: Compare the forms and ideas of the two texts.

a.best: It gives your writing an area of ideas to explore

b.best: One framework can lead to very different texts

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('can'). The three distractors all use absolutes ('must', 'only'), so a test-savvy student could pick the answer without understanding frameworks.

b.q: Priya and Tom both build their texts around the framework of play. Priya writes a story about a childhood cricket game. Tom writes a speech about why adults need time to be playful. What does this show?
